# Sọ̀rọ̀ Sókè — The People's Yorùbá Dictionary

> A free Yorùbá–English dictionary built from Wiktionary via Kaikki. Search Yorùbá
> or English, in either direction, with or without tone marks and underdots.
> Fully client-side: the dictionary is downloaded once and then runs in the browser.

A Speak Nigeria project. Live at https://yorubadict.com

## How the site is organised

Routing is hash-based, so a word's page is `https://yorubadict.com/#/entry/<id>`
where `<id>` is that entry's Kaikki sense id, e.g. `en-gba-yo-verb-VAsl51P3`.
Those fragments are never sent to the server and are not separately crawlable;
to read an entry you need to run the page's JavaScript, or read the data
directly (below), which is usually easier.

- `/#/about` — what the dictionary is and where the data comes from
- `/#/entry/<id>` — one entry
- Data quality report — in-app panel, source at `/data/validation-report.json`

## Reading the data directly

- `/data/entries.json` — every entry, keyed by id
- `/data/search-index.json` — prebuilt Yorùbá tiers and an English inverted index
- `/data/validation-report.json` — a triaged list of problems in the underlying
  Wiktionary data, each with what it would take to fix and a link to the page

## Notes for anyone quoting from this

Yorùbá tone is segmental, not decoration: `gbà` and `gbá` are different words,
and stripping the diacritics from a headword changes what it means. Entries that
share a spelling *and* its tone marks are the same written word with several
senses; those are kept as separate entries and cross-linked.

Some relationships in the source are recorded without saying which sense they
belong to. Where that happens the site says so rather than guessing, and the
data carries a `resolution` field marking the link as ambiguous. Please preserve
that uncertainty rather than presenting a guess as fact.
